observations.evidence: The left edge of the WB carriageway is a raised kerb of a wide grass median with trees, running from about (265,375) to the lower-left (about (0,500)). The opposing carriageway lies beyond the median, not beside the WB lanes.
A solid white longitudinal line on the right runs from about (340,338) to (530,640), separating the general traffic lane from a narrow strip along the right kerb.

A narrow strip (roughly a bicycle-lane width, leaves along the gutter) lies between the solid white line and the right kerb. It looks like a bicycle lane or shoulder; no bicycle symbol or sign is visible in this view to confirm it.
The right kerb (granite kerb, then a brick band and concrete sidewalk with trees and lamp posts) runs from about (350,340) to (640,540).

At the camera position no lane line is visible between the median kerb and the solid white line, so this cross-section shows one wide general lane. Tree shadows across the near pavement could hide very faint paint.

Far ahead a new white lane line begins at about (297-312, 337-355), between the median side and the right line. This suggests the carriageway splits into two lanes nearer the junction (an added lane or turn pocket downstream of this position).
A faint white pavement marking far ahead at about (262-292, 349-353), left of where the new lane line starts, is too distant to read (it could be an arrow or a word). No direction is assigned.
Beyond the median on the left: the opposing carriageway with parked/moving cars (about 0-194, 329-352), its far sidewalk and buildings. It does not belong to the WB approach.

Strong tree shadows cover the near pavement, and the distant section near the junction is small and partly hidden by vehicles (dark car about 289-305, 324-337), so markings near the stop bar cannot be read.

notes: Image dated 2020-11 (autumn), about 104 m from the junction centre (far sampling position); it may not reflect later restriping.

At this cross-section the WB side is a median-divided carriageway with one wide general lane plus a narrow kerbside strip. A lane split begins further ahead, but where it starts and what movement it serves cannot be read here.
No arrows are legible; nothing is inferred from vehicles or signals.
